page: Microsoft Azure E2bs_v6 is an x86_64 virtualization instance belonging to the memory-optimized Ebsv6 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel processor alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile yields an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, aligning with memory-intensive workloads that require substantial operating memory relative to core compute capacity. Hardware accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero.

Storage configuration on the E2bs_v6 provides no local disk capacity, requiring workloads to rely exclusively on remote persistent volumes. The instance is designed for Premium Storage integration and specialized remote block storage performance, allowing it to decouple persistent storage requirements from compute lifecycles. Networking configurations do not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external configuration for public egress or ingress.

The absence of local disks reduces data loss risk associated with ephemeral storage and maintains cost efficiency for systems backed entirely by managed block storage. With a 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio, the E2bs_v6 is appropriate for relational database engines, in-memory caching solutions, light enterprise resource planning services, and middle-tier enterprise applications with significant memory footprints but modest processing demands.
description: Microsoft Azure E2bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and x86_64 Intel processor architecture. Configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, suiting operations requiring high memory headroom relative to CPU throughput. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage and optimized remote block storage performance. Graphical acceleration is absent, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By prioritizing memory capacity and dedicated CPU allocation over high core counts, the E2bs_v6 provides balanced cost efficiency for memory-centric, remote-storage-dependent deployments. Suitable workloads include small relational database instances, in-memory key-value stores, business intelligence processing, and enterprise application hosting.
